title: Gently Poached Prawns with Classic Cocktail Sauce
summary: Plump king prawns gently poached in aromatic water, chilled and served around glasses of tangy horseradish cocktail sauce. A cool, elegant starter that can be prepared ahead.
equipment: large saucepan with a lid (3-4 litres)

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
ingredients.note: about ¾ tsp; dissolved in the water

ingredients.item: hot pepper sauce (check the label for alcohol)
lemon, cut into wedges, to serve

steps.title: Devein in the shell
steps.text: Using kitchen scissors, snip along the back of each prawn shell and pull out the dark vein, leaving the shell in place. The shell shields the delicate flesh during cooking and adds flavour to the poaching liquid.

steps.title: Start from cold
steps.text: Put the prawns, cold water, salt, bay leaves, peppercorns and celery seeds into the saucepan, then squeeze in the lemon and drop in the halves. Heat over medium heat, stirring now and then, for 6-8 minutes until the water reaches 77°C and the prawns begin to turn pink. Starting cold heats the prawns slowly and evenly, so they stay tender.

steps.title: Rest off the heat
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat, cover and leave for 5-7 minutes until the prawns are pink all over, firm and opaque right through. Cut one in half to check; the centre should read at least 63°C. Gentle residual heat finishes them without the rubbery texture that rapid boiling causes.

steps.title: Chill and peel
steps.text: Tip the ice into the pan to stop the cooking and leave for 5 minutes until the prawns are cold. Drain, peel them, leaving the tails on, and refrigerate until serving, for up to 24 hours. Quick chilling halts carryover cooking and keeps the texture plump.

steps.title: Mix the sauce
steps.text: Stir together the ketchup, horseradish, lemon juice, hot sauce and cayenne. Taste, adding more horseradish if you like a sharper kick. Its sharp heat cuts through the sweetness of the ketchup and the prawns.

steps.title: Assemble the glasses
steps.text: Spoon the sauce into the glasses and hang the prawns around the rims. Serve well chilled with lemon wedges.

tips: A common mistake is boiling the prawns hard, which makes them tough; bring the water up gently and let the residual heat do the rest.
Leaving the tails on gives your guests a handy grip for dipping.
Check both the horseradish and hot sauce labels for alcohol.
Make the sauce a few hours ahead so the flavours can mingle in the fridge.
storage: Keep the prawns and sauce chilled and eat within 24 hours. Do not leave them out of the fridge for more than 2 hours. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
